prompts.name: Conservative File Preservation and Cherry-Pick Closeout
prompts.sprintRole: Audit unexpected deletions and unfinished agent work, preserve unique files and commits, and integrate only validated changes
prompts.useWhen: An agent run ended, crashed, changed branches, removed many files, triggered a OneDrive or sync-provider bulk-delete warning, or left uncertain work that must be classified, preserved, committed, and selectively cherry-picked before cleanup.
prompts.inspectFirst: Repository root and origin, current branch and worktrees, git status porcelain output, tracked deletions, untracked files, ignored/generated policy, recent commits, reflog, stashes, open PRs, sync-root location, pending OneDrive or SharePoint deletion warnings, validators, and prior run evidence.
prompts.expectedOutput: A committed preservation closeout with a machine-readable file disposition ledger, recovered unique work on an isolated recovery branch, validated cherry-picks into the intended target when authorized, explicit keep/delete decisions, and proof that no unexplained files were discarded.
prompts.nextStep: Open the preservation ledger and exact Git diff, then execute only the recorded validated cherry-pick or cleanup command; leave every disputed item preserved until an operator resolves it.
prompts.proofGate: Every missing, deleted, untracked, ignored, or branch-only item is classified; unique work is committed before integration; cherry-picks name source and destination SHAs; validators pass; sync-provider bulk deletion is not approved without a matching manifest; and final Git state, retained artifacts, and remaining disputes are reported.
prompts.copyContent:
PRESERVE AND CLOSE OUT THE AGENT WORK NOW. DO NOT DELETE, RESET, CLEAN, OR APPROVE A SYNC-PROVIDER BULK DELETION UNTIL EVERY AFFECTED ITEM IS CLASSIFIED.

Repo: resolve and print the exact repository root and canonical origin.
Branch or PR: resolve from Git and GitHub evidence.
Sprint: Conservative File Preservation and Cherry-Pick Closeout.
Lane: recovery, preservation, and bounded integration.
Owned scope: uncertain deletions, untracked or ignored work, interrupted agent changes, recovery branches, preservation manifests, focused validation, and authorized cherry-picks.
Forbidden scope: force-push, default-branch rewriting, git reset --hard, git clean -fd/-fdx, broad Remove-Item -Recurse -Force or rm -rf, OneDrive/SharePoint bulk-delete approval without a matching manifest, secret capture, and unrelated refactors.
Expected artifacts: pre-action evidence, file-disposition ledger, recovery commit SHAs, cherry-pick ledger when applicable, validator output, final Git status, and one exact next command.

SAFETY DEFAULT
When intent is uncertain, preserve. A OneDrive, SharePoint, Dropbox, or other sync-provider large-delete warning is a failed safety gate until repository evidence explains the exact deletion set. Do not select Delete all items merely because an earlier agent probably intended it. Keep or pause the disputed deletion set, preserve evidence, and classify it first.

1. RESOLVE THE WORKSPACE
- Print repository root, origin URL, current branch, HEAD SHA, upstream, worktrees, and whether the path is inside OneDrive, SharePoint, Dropbox, Desktop backup, or another synchronized root.
- Run git status --porcelain=v2 --branch, git diff --name-status, git diff --cached --name-status, git ls-files --deleted, git ls-files --others --exclude-standard, git log --oneline --decorate -10, git reflog -20, and git stash list.
- Inspect open PRs and recent branches before assuming a file is obsolete.
- Do not alter the current working tree during evidence collection.

2. BUILD A FILE-DISPOSITION LEDGER
Create a tracked or approved ignored JSON/CSV/Markdown ledger with one row per affected path and these fields:
- path
- repository root or outside-repo location
- Git state: tracked modified, tracked deleted, staged, untracked, ignored, branch-only, generated, or unknown
- source branch, commit, PR, reflog entry, or run evidence
- expected owner or artifact family
- classification: KEEP, RECOVER, CHERRY-PICK, REGENERATE, DELETE-CANDIDATE, or DISPUTED
- reason and evidence
- intended destination
- validator
- disposition status
Never classify by filename alone. Compare contents, hashes, Git history, registry/manifests, generators, and current target-branch equivalents.

3. PRESERVE UNIQUE WORK BEFORE CLEANUP
- Treat any unique tracked change, untracked source file, prompt, manifest, validator, script, report, or operator artifact as recoverable until proven disposable.
- Create an isolated recovery branch or worktree from the recorded floor.
- Copy or restore only the classified unique work into that recovery lane.
- Remove secrets and machine-local junk from the commit set without destroying the original evidence.
- Run focused checks and commit coherent recovery units with descriptive messages.
- Record each recovery commit SHA and the paths it preserves.
- Do not use a stash as the only durable preservation record.

4. DISTINGUISH VALID DELETIONS FROM LOSS
A deletion may become DELETE-CANDIDATE only when evidence shows one of these:
- the target branch intentionally removed the tracked path and replacement behavior is present and validated;
- the file is reproducible generated output covered by a tracked generator and regeneration check;
- the file is documented disposable evidence or cache under the correct ignored path;
- the content is an exact duplicate already preserved by a named commit or artifact.
Anything else remains KEEP, RECOVER, or DISPUTED.

5. CHERRY-PICK SELECTIVELY
- Inspect candidate commits and diffs before integration.
- Cherry-pick only coherent commits whose owned scope belongs on the destination branch.
- Preserve source SHA, destination SHA, files, dependency order, conflicts, and validation in the ledger.
- When a source branch mixes useful and unrelated work, create a clean recovery commit first instead of cherry-picking the mixed commit blindly.
- Never close or abandon the source PR/branch until all unique useful work is preserved or explicitly rejected with evidence.

6. VALIDATE BEFORE ANY DELETE OR CLOSE ACTION
Run focused validators for recovered files, then repository checks in the declared order, git diff --check, generated-output hygiene, secret scanning where available, and final comparison against the destination branch.
For a sync-provider warning, compare the provider's affected count and visible paths against the ledger. If the counts or paths do not reconcile, do not approve deletion.

7. CLOSE OUT WITH PROOF
Report:
- repo, branch/worktree, PR, and recorded floor
- whether the path is synchronized
- affected counts by classification
- ledger path
- recovered files and commit SHAs
- cherry-picked source and destination SHAs
- regenerated outputs
- delete candidates not yet executed
- disputed items
- validators and exact results
- skipped checks and why
- final git status
- push or PR state
- proof level and proof ceiling
- one exact next command

A response that says the files are probably safe to delete, silently cleans the worktree, approves a bulk sync deletion without reconciliation, or closes a branch before preserving unique work is invalid.
